title: Vectors: Dynamic Collections
learningObjectives: Describe relevant storage, indexing and size rules.
Trace a collection operation or traversal.
Recognize bounds, lifetime or input pitfalls.
Apply the type to a practical collection task.

understand.concept: std::vector is a dynamically sized sequence. push_back adds elements; size and empty describe the collection.
understand.whyItMatters: Vectors fit collections whose size changes at runtime.
understand.explain: Check bounds, emptiness, and iterator/reference invalidation after growth.

examples.title: Grow vector
examples.explanation: push_back appends and grows the collection.

examples.title: Empty test
examples.explanation: empty is true before any items are added.

examples.title: Remove final item
examples.explanation: pop_back removes the last item; call only when non-empty.

practise.guidedTask: Trace all five Vectors: Dynamic Collections examples. Record sizes, indexes, values and condition checks. Identify first/last valid element and relevant edge cases.
practise.independentTask: Create a small C++ data-processing program demonstrating vectors: dynamic collections. Test typical values, empty/boundary cases, and invalid input or indexing where relevant. Explain why this collection is appropriate.
hints: Use zero-based indexes and verify bounds.
Prefer range-based traversal when index is unnecessary.
Check emptiness before operations such as front or pop_back.
Test first, last and invalid boundaries.

questions.explanation: Removing from an empty vector is invalid.
